local.h: Decatur Book Festival cuts ties with bookstore
local.b: The Decatur Book Festival broke ties with Kiss and Tale Romance Bookshop after a festival-goer alleged racism on social media.
more: The 21st annual festival was held Oct. 2-3 in downtown Decatur.

local.h: All six lost in Nantucket air ambulance named
local.b: Officials identified the six people aboard the air ambulance that crashed off Nantucket on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.
more: Passengers were Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and her son Sergio Wayne Lottimore, 41, of Bermuda; the four crew were Canadian.
The Coast Guard suspended its search Sunday after 66 hours.

local.h: Jury selection begins in Birchmore murder trial
local.b: Jury selection starts in the trial of former Stoughton detective Matthew Farwell, accused of killing Sandra Birchmore in 2021.
more: Prosecutors say he abused her from age 15 in a police youth program, then killed her to keep her from reporting it.
Farwell has pleaded not guilty and maintains she took her own life.

local.h: Question 9 puts Mass. gun law to voters
local.b: Massachusetts voters will decide whether to keep or repeal the state's 2024 gun law.
more: Gov. Healey called it the state's most significant gun safety law in a decade.
It set the state's first rules on untraceable 'ghost guns.'

local.h: Question 6 would fund nature conservation
local.b: Question 6 asks voters to dedicate existing sales tax on outdoor gear to a 'Nature for All' land conservation fund.
more: Massachusetts aims to protect 30% of its land and waters by 2030.

goodnews.b: Franklin Park's Scarboro Hill will become home to the White Pine Gathering Place, a monument designed by and for the Wampanoag people.
more: City officials say it will be Boston's first permanent monument dedicated to an Indigenous community.
Organizers say it will give tribal communities a space for ceremony and healing.

local.h: Pritzker lost 80 pounds with GLP-1 drug
local.b: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker says he lost 80 pounds since spring 2024 with help from a GLP-1 medication.
more: He was diagnosed with prediabetes, then Type 2 diabetes.
GLP-1s can treat more than diabetes and obesity but carry risks.

local.h: Suits seek air data after Lineage warehouse fire
local.b: Advocacy groups sued the EPA and the city of Los Angeles for records on possible toxic emissions from the Lineage warehouse fire in Boyle Heights, LAist reports.
more: California Communities Against Toxics says large amounts of ammonia have leaked since the fire destroyed the refrigeration system.

local.h: LA food bank strains as CalFresh cuts bite
local.b: Community Space Food Bank now sees 30 to 40 new people a day, up from two to 10, as CalFresh benefits are cut or end, LAist reports.
more: Founders Gaines and Hang Newborn are raising money to keep it open and buy its building.

local.h: LAUSD at high risk of insolvency, state finds
local.b: California's school finance watchdog says LA Unified is at high risk of insolvency by 2028.
more: The agency cited overspending, falling enrollment and rising costs.

local.h: Trump remark on Iran hitting LA draws fire
local.b: Trump mused at a Nebraska rally that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego, drawing criticism.
more: The White House said he meant he wants to keep Iran from having that capability.

local.h: ICE arrests near 40,000 across NY and NJ
local.b: ICE has made more than 19,500 arrests in New York state and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during Trump's second term, Gothamist reports from new government data.
more: The arrests are largely of Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories.

local.h: Crashes pile up on Central Park's car-free loop
local.b: Three people have died in crashes on Central Park's 6-mile loop since June as more than 100,000 people use the park each day, Gothamist reports.
more: On Monday a 71-year-old cyclist fell near 84th Street while avoiding an off-leash dog.

local.h: NYC to spend $9M on youth gender-affirming care
local.b: New York City plans to spend nearly $9 million on local groups providing gender-affirming care to minors, part of a $15 million Mamdani administration pledge.
more: It follows deals by NYU Langone and Mount Sinai with the Trump administration to stop such care for minors.

local.h: Mamdani names Rikers oversight board chair
local.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani named re-entry advocate Christopher Watler to chair the city's jail oversight board.
more: Watler has spent decades building re-entry and diversion programs.

local.h: Loophole helps Hochul, Blakeman raise millions
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul and GOP challenger Bruce Blakeman are using a quirk in state law to raise millions of dollars.

local.h: Police name suspects in off-duty cop stabbing
local.b: Commissioner Jessica Tisch identified two men police believe stabbed an off-duty NYPD officer in a Bronx robbery last week.
more: Police named D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24.

local.h: NYC weighs expanding Cannonsville Reservoir
local.b: The city may expand the Cannonsville Reservoir, its third-largest drinking water source, after a drought two years ago.
more: The drought cut the city's water supply to worryingly low levels.

local.h: Legionella found in Staten Island complex
local.b: Legionella bacteria were found in a Staten Island apartment complex's water system after two residents got sick.

local.h: NYC fears migrants will skip health care
local.b: City health officials worry green card rule changes will lead some immigrants to avoid Medicaid and other benefits.

local.h: Bronx woman dies, baby critical after balcony fall
local.b: A Bronx woman died and a baby girl is in critical condition after they fell from a balcony early Tuesday, police said.
more: Someone called 911 from a building at Ollinville and Allerton avenues around 3:38 a.m.

local.h: Relief for NYC tenants losing rent vouchers
local.b: Nearly 6,300 NYC households losing federal rental aid may get to replace their vouchers and stay in their apartments.
more: HUD issued new guidance after letting the earlier aid expire caused fear among tenants and landlords.

local.h: Drought leaves 94,000 in France without tap water
local.b: France's environment ministry says 94,000 people are on emergency drinking water supplies due to severe drought, up from 64,000 in early September.
more: Another 6.4 million residents are on water systems placed on alert.

local.h: France suspends stun grenades at school protests
local.b: France suspended police use of stun grenades at high school protests after a teenager lost his hand to one.
more: Many high schools stay closed for the rest of the week.
Student leaders plan an 'act four' of protests on Thursday.

local.h: France halts high school classes amid protests
local.b: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu suspended high school classes for the rest of the week as protesters clashed with police, including in Paris.
more: Officials counted about 250,000 protesters nationwide; organizers said about half a million.
Lecornu said 'burning down a high school does not improve the state of high school buildings.'

local.h: French unions call nationwide strike Nov. 5
local.b: French unions called a day of cross-sector strikes and protests on Thursday, November 5th.
more: The CFDT, CGT, FO, Unsa and FSU unions back the call 'for wages, public services, employment and industry.'
The government faces growing opposition to its draft 2027 budget.

local.h: Ferry sick-out strands thousands of riders
local.b: Thousands of Puget Sound ferry riders were stranded Monday as major routes and dozens of sailings were canceled.
more: Nearly two dozen engine room workers called out sick and backup crews declined to fill in.
Their union blamed Washington State Ferries' failure to hire more staff.

local.h: Bellingham man charged with aiding BC shooter
local.b: A Bellingham resident is charged with helping the shooter who killed eight people at Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in February.
more: Federal prosecutors in Seattle announced the arrest with the FBI and RCMP.

local.h: Orca mom J31 carries dead calf again
local.b: Endangered southern resident orca J31 was seen carrying a dead newborn on her nose in the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
more: She did the same in 2016 and has lost at least eight other offspring.
She has one living daughter, now 7.

local.h: Mayor Wilson explains budget without tax hike
local.b: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson explained why she relied on cuts, not a JumpStart payroll tax increase, to close a roughly $175 million gap.
more: Her $9.1 billion budget proposal is now before the City Council, which will amend it.
